supported_environment.os: Parrot OS 6.4 MATE Security Edition (VirtualBox VM on Windows host)

commands.provision: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install jsonschema pytest pyyaml reportlab
commands.build: python3 vendor-verifier/cli.py && python3 generate_reports.py && python3 generate_memo.py
commands.clean: rm -f evidence-verdicts.json data-flow.graphml vendor-risk-memo.pdf contradiction-matrix.csv evidence-index.csv vendor-risk-register.csv monitoring-plan.yaml generated/test-report.xml

known_limitations: RESOLVED before submission: an early file-handling discrepancy affecting five input files was identified and resolved before analysis began, with no effect on any downstream verdict or decision.
subprocessor.assurance treats a present-but-self-attested assurance value the same as a missing one; this is a documented interpretive judgment, not a schema fact (see evidence-index.csv).
The undisclosed-subprocessor extension check joins telemetry subprocessors to the DPA-disclosed list on name/id only, the only join key supplied in the pack.

RESOLVED before submission (fix #1): an earlier revision of decision.py and generate_reports.py had assigned-case entity names (subprocessor names, one deletion job id, one access event id) typed as literal strings in condition/report text rather than derived from the verdicts passed in, which would have failed to update on a replacement export. Fixed by deriving all entity references live via regex extraction from verdict locators/messages; proven with a swap drill (tests/test_decision_no_hardcoded_entities.py) that renames every referenced entity and asserts none of the original names survive regeneration.

RESOLVED before submission (fix #2, found on review of fix #1): pipeline.py separately hard-coded a literal SOC 2 exception id ('EX-CC7.2') as a no-fallback next(...) lookup; renumbering that id in a replacement export raised an unhandled StopIteration and crashed the entire pipeline rather than just showing stale text -- a strictly worse failure. Fixed by matching on the exception's stable `condition` field instead of its arbitrary `id` label, and by degrading to an `insufficient` verdict (never a crash, never a silent pass) if no matching exception exists. Proven with tests/test_decision_no_hardcoded_entities.py's second test and a standing structural test (tests/test_no_unsafe_lookups.py) that statically scans every vendor-verifier module for the same bare-next()-with-no-default pattern and for literal case-specific values used as comparison targets, so a third instance of this bug class is caught automatically rather than requiring another manual review.
